lines.trans: Hi, Ilona. These flowers are for you.
What strange flowers!
If you want, I will buy others?
Listen, what do you need?
I already told you.
Let me drop by your place this evening.
Men usually court women.
I am also trying to court.
Then invite me to the movies.
Let's go right this evening.
Today I am working. Tomorrow I can.
Alright, let's go tomorrow.
Just not to an action movie!
I love romantic movies.
Agreed, I will choose a movie.

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'action movie, blockbuster' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Just not to an action movie!
In the evening we watched an American action movie.

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: до вечера = until the evening; вечером = in the evening
E.g. a school evening. Common masculine noun meaning 'evening' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!

meanings.en: to choose, select; to use up completely (quotas, limits)
meanings.note: + acc. Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'брать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to choose, use up', paired with 'выбирать'.

examples.text: В этом году все квоты выбрали.
examples.trans: This year all the quotas have been used up.
She chose the most beautiful dress.
Agreed, I will choose a movie.

meanings.note: давай + 1st person plural or infinitive
давай + 1st person plural or infinitive

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.en: to agree, to come to an arrangement
meanings.note: 'договоримся' = we'll work something out

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('other, another, different').
Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('other, another, different').

examples.text: Послушайте, а можно в другое место? Здесь плохо пахнет.
examples.trans: Listen, could we go somewhere else? It smells bad in here.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'woman' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Твоя жена очень мудрая женщина. Ты её слушай.
examples.trans: Your wife is a very wise woman. You listen to her.

meanings.note: Спасибо за + accusative. Core Russian prep meaning 'for; behind' in everyday speech.
+ instrumental. Core Russian prep meaning 'for; behind' in everyday speech.
Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втра').

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

заскочить.gloss: to drop by, to pop in

meanings.en: to drop by, to visit briefly
meanings.note: Informal call on someone. Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'скочить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to drop by, to pop in', paired with 'заскакивать'.

examples.text: Давай я к тебе заскочу вечером.
examples.trans: Let me drop by your place this evening.

examples.text: Я заскочу в магазин за хлебом на пять минут.
examples.trans: I'll pop into the shop for bread for five minutes.

meanings.note: + dative. Core Russian prep meaning 'to, towards' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: In questions. Core Russian det meaning 'what; what a' in everyday speech.
in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Film theater or cinematic art. Common neuter noun meaning 'cinema, movies, film' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Then invite me to the movies.
So, let's look at the schedule in the cinema.

examples.text: Зачем ты вообще ведёшь её в кино?
examples.trans: Why are you even taking her to the movies?

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to buy', paired with 'покупать'.

examples.text: Юле бы дублёнку купили, Славику бы ноутбук.
examples.trans: We could have bought Yulia a sheepskin coat, and Slavik a laptop.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to love, to like', paired with 'полюбить'.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to love, to like', paired with 'полюбить'.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: + infinitive. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: adult male; declines like a feminine -а noun

examples.text: У мужчины бывает не только жена.
examples.trans: A man can have more than just a wife.
This man is waiting for you.

examples.text: У мужчины, мальчик, бывает не только жена. Это моя девушка.
examples.trans: A man, my boy, can have more than just a wife. She's my girlfriend.

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.
+ accusative: на второй срок. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Надо + infinitive. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ычно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: А в каких местах он обычно пьёт?
examples.trans: And in what places does he usually drink?

examples.text: Он обычно встаёт в семь утра.
examples.trans: He usually gets up at seven in the morning.

meanings.note: On foot. Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to go (set off)', paired with 'идти'.

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

meanings.en: to have a look, to take a look
meanings.note: One completed look. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'смотреть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to have a look', paired with 'смотреть'.
Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'смотреть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to have a look', paired with 'смотреть'.

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: Informal: family and friends. Core Russian interj meaning 'hi' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'гласить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to invite, to call in', paired with 'приглашать'.

meanings.en: to call in (a witness, a guest)
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'гласить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to invite, to call in', paired with 'приглашать'.
Прямо так = just like that. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: В смысле, Виктор Степанович? Прямо так, да?
examples.trans: What do you mean, Viktor Stepanovich? Just like that?

meanings.en: to try, to attempt, to make an effort
meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to try, to attempt', paired with 'попытаться'.

examples.trans: He tried to explain the situation.

examples.text: Пыталась? С бутылкой вина в руке?
examples.trans: You tried? With a bottle of wine in your hand?

meanings.note: работать + instrumental = to work as: работать мэром

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Relational adjective formed with the Slavic suffix '-ский' ('pertaining to'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('romantic').

examples.text: Дарят папе романтический ужин на двоих.
examples.trans: They're giving Dad a romantic dinner for two.
This is a very romantic place.

examples.text: Кстати, звонили из итальянского ресторана. Дарят папе романтический ужин на двоих.
examples.trans: By the way, they called from the Italian restaurant. They're giving Dad a romantic dinner for two.

meanings.note: The г sounds like в. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодня').

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?

Polite request. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to say, to tell', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: + accusative. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лушать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to listen', paired with 'послушать'.
the imperative 'слушай' starts a sentence, like 'look, ...'

'Слушаю' = I'm listening. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'лушать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to listen', paired with 'послушать'.

examples.text: Слушай, Самсон, я тут подумал. Твой начальник — такой опытный специалист.
examples.trans: Listen, Samson, I've been thinking. Your boss is such an experienced specialist.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'транный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('strange, odd').
At that time. Core Russian adv meaning 'then, back then' in everyday speech.
Core Russian adv meaning 'then, back then' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'too, also' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы же здесь выросли. И о людях тоже надо думать.
examples.trans: After all, we grew up here. And you have to think about people too.

meanings.note: softens a request: только не сердись = just don't be angry
One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.

ухаживать.gloss: to court, to woo; to look after

meanings.en: to court, to pay court to
meanings.note: + за + instrumental. Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'хаживать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to court, to woo; to look after'.

meanings.en: to look after, to care for
meanings.note: + за + instrumental. Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'хаживать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to court, to woo; to look after'.

examples.text: Он за мной после концерта ухаживал.
examples.trans: He courted me after a concert once.
She looks after her sick mother.

examples.text: Он за мной после концерта ухаживал. В Москву звал замуж!
examples.trans: He courted me after a concert once. He asked me to marry him and come to Moscow!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'movie, film' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я всегда смотрел фильмы про войну.
examples.trans: I always watched movies about the war.

meanings.note: How something is done. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
As an answer. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
+ infinitive or a noun. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: plural цветы is used for cut flowers / a bouquet
Question word. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Conjunction. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Linking word: главное — это народ. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'I' in everyday speech.
The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Plural все. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good, nice').

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.
